rows.version_read: v2, 19 Mar 2026 (full text, pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25116v2)
rows.cite: Thomas Hou, Yixuan Wang, Changhe Yang -- Nonuniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions to the unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes Equation
rows.equation_certified: The forward self-similar profile system (1.12) for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equation on R^3, jointly with its linearised eigenvalue problem: '-1/2 U~ - 1/2 xi.grad U~ + Pi(U~.grad U~) - Delta U~ = 0, div U~ = 0' and '-1/2 v~ - 1/2 xi.grad v~ + Pi(U~.grad v~ + v~.grad U~) - Delta v~ = lambda~ v~'.
rows.dissipative_term_evidence: Proposition 1 (Exact self-similar profile), eq. (1.15), p.5: 'there exists a U_bar satisfying the following equation in the distributional sense: -1/2 U_bar - 1/2 xi.grad U_bar - Delta U_bar + Pi(U.grad U_bar + U_bar.grad U + U_bar.grad U_bar) = -Pi E_U, div U_bar = 0 ... so that U~ = U + U_bar solves the first and third equations of (1.12). Moreover, the perturbation U_bar in H^1 satisfies ||U_bar||_{L^2} <~ eps_U.' The Laplacian is a term of the very equation the enclosure solves.
rows.interval_arithmetic_evidence: Section 7.3, p.55: 'All pointwise evaluations f_{i,j} are computed with interval arithmetic to enclose round-off.' Section 7.4: 'with interval arithmetic capturing floating-point uncertainty.' Section 7 opening, p.53: 'In this section, we outline the framework we use for rigorous computer-assisted validation; in particular, the rigorous justification for the constants in Section 4.5.'
rows.fluid_evidence: Section 1, eq. (1.1), p.1: 'partial_t u + u.grad u - Delta u + grad p = 0, div u = 0, u(t=0,x) = u_in(x)' -- 'the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equation on the whole space without forcing'. Transport nonlinearity AND incompressibility, both present in the certified profile system.
rows.not_a_blowup_quoted_verbatim: 'The readers should not confuse this self-similar setting, which starts from singular initial data, with the backward self-similar setting related to finite-time singularities from smooth initial data.'
rows.not_a_blowup_location: Section 1.2 'Self-similar setting', p.2, immediately after eq. (1.5)
rows.not_a_blowup_corroboration: Theorem 1, p.2: 'There exist infinitely many distinct suitable Leray-Hopf solutions to the Navier-Stokes equation (1.1) on R^3 x [0,1] with the same divergence-free initial condition u_in = u_loc of compact support ... The solutions are L^s([0,1];L^q(R^3)), for any q >= 2, 3/q + 2/s > 1, and smooth for positive times.' The theorem's conclusion is NONUNIQUENESS, not a finite-time singularity; the certified solutions are smooth for t>0.

rows.version_read: v2, 22 Jul 2026 (full text, pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/2605.19716v2, 101 pp.)
rows.cite: Feng Shao, Dongyi Wei, Ping Zhang, Zhifei Zhang -- Self-similar blow-up solutions of d-dimensional incompressible Euler equations with C^{1,(1-2/d)-} velocity
rows.equation_certified: NOTHING IS CERTIFIED BY INTERVAL ARITHMETIC. The object constructed is a self-similar profile of the d-dimensional axisymmetric incompressible EULER equations without swirl, eq. (1.1), obtained by a purely analytic fixed-point argument.
rows.fluid_evidence: Section 1, eq. (1.1), p.2: 'u_t + u.grad u + grad P = 0, (t,x) in [0,T) x R^d, div u = 0, u|_{t=0} = u_0' -- 'the velocity field of a perfect incompressible fluid'. Transport nonlinearity and incompressibility: fluid, unambiguously.
rows.failing_clause_quoted: In contrast to [11,12], our construction of self-similar profiles is purely analytic and does not rely on any computer-assisted verification.
rows.failing_clause_second_quoted: u_t + u . grad u + grad P = 0, (t,x) in [0,T) x R^d, div u = 0
rows.failing_clause_second_location: Section 1, eq. (1.1), p.2 -- the equation carries NO dissipative term at all: it is Euler, not Navier-Stokes.
rows.grade_a_fails_twice: Clause (Grade A) fails on BOTH of its constituents: (i) there is no interval-arithmetic certificate anywhere in the paper, by the authors' own explicit statement; (ii) even hypothetically, the equation the profile solves is inviscid Euler and carries no dissipative term.
rows.singularity_evidence: Theorem 1.3 (Finite-energy blow-up), p.6: 'there exists T>0 so that the system (1.1) has an axisymmetric swirl-free solution u : [0,T) x R^d -> R^d'; Remark 1.2(1): 'the blow-up solutions constructed in Theorem 1.1 do not possess finite kinetic energy ... This permits suitable truncation procedures to yield asymptotically self-similar blow-up solutions'.

rows.version_read: v1, 14 May 2026 (full text, pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/2605.15149v1, ~91 pp.)
rows.cite: Jiajie Chen -- Asymptotically self-similar blowup for 3D incompressible Euler with C^{1,1/3-} velocity I: C^infty 1D limiting profiles
rows.equation_certified: The one-parameter family of 1D models for the 3D axisymmetric incompressible EULER equation, eq. (1.1): 'partial_t omega + 2 psi_alpha partial_x omega = -(1-alpha) partial_x psi_alpha omega, psi_alpha(omega)(x) = - integral_R |x-y|^alpha omega(y) dy'. Interval arithmetic (INTLAB) IS genuinely used.
rows.interval_arithmetic_evidence: Appendix B.3 'Interval Arithmetic', p.~68: 'For the rigorous computer-assisted proof, we use interval arithmetic [41,43] ... in INTLAB'. Section 1.5: 'The computer-assisted estimates are confined to Section 3, Section 4.3-4.4, and Appendices B-C'.
rows.fluid_evidence: Section 1, p.1: 'The model (1.1) was derived in [11,35] to describe the behavior of the 3D axisymmetric Euler without swirl near the symmetry axis, with C^alpha vorticity. Here psi_alpha models the angular stream function, omega models the angular vorticity'. Transport nonlinearity present; fluid-adjacent by leg 174's own field definition.
rows.failing_clause_quoted: partial_t omega + 2 psi_alpha partial_x omega = -(1-alpha) partial_x psi_alpha omega, psi_alpha(omega)(x) = - integral_R |x-y|^alpha omega(y) dy
rows.failing_clause_location: Section 1, eq. (1.1), p.1 -- the certified equation carries NO dissipative term. The words 'viscosity', 'Laplacian' and 'Navier-Stokes' occur nowhere in the paper's own equations; the only occurrence of 'Navier-Stokes' in the body (p.7, literature survey) is a citation of OTHER authors' work, namely [34] = arXiv:2509.25116.

rows.version_read: v1, 10 Apr 2026 (full text, pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/2604.09949v1, 14 pp.)
rows.cite: Rishad Shahmurov -- Stable Finite-Time Singularity Formation in 3D Navier-Stokes via 5D-Lifted Axisymmetric Reductions
rows.equation_certified: The 5D-lifted stationary rescaled profile equation G(Omega_bar, nu) = 0, eq. (6)-(7), p.2: 'G(Omega_bar, nu) := Omega_bar + (1/2)(rho d_rho + zeta d_zeta) Omega_bar + b_bar.grad Omega_bar - nu (d_rho rho Omega_bar + (3/rho) d_rho Omega_bar + d_zeta zeta Omega_bar) + 2 (u_bar_rho / rho) Omega_bar'. On its face this equation DOES carry the dissipative term (the nu-bracket) and IS fluid (5D-lifted axisymmetric NS swirl equation).
rows.grade_a_fails_by: REFUTATION, NOT BY THE CLAUSE'S FACE. The certificate cannot enclose 'a solution' because the object it claims to reconstruct is proved not to exist.
rows.failing_clause_quoted: u(x, t) = (1 / sqrt(T* - t)) u_bar( x / sqrt(T* - t) )
rows.failing_clause_location: Theorem 12.1 (Singular solution recovery), eq. (18), Section 12 'Blow-up Reconstruction', p.11
rows.failing_clause_why: That display is, verbatim, the definition of an exact BACKWARD self-similar solution of 3D Navier-Stokes on R^3, with the profile space forcing u_bar in L^3(R^3) and stronger -- exactly the class Necas-Ruzicka-Sverak (Acta Math. 176, 1996) and Tsai (ARMA 143, 1998) prove must be trivial. The manuscript never cites, engages, or attempts to evade that 30-year-old exclusion theorem.
